newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian banks push for lower interest rates.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian banks push for lower interest rates.

text.p: Slovenia's Association of Banks said on Thursday it had pushed its members for a new agreement on a ceiling for bank deposit rates, which would reduce the top rate to 1.5 from two percent.
The new accord is expected to be enforced from April 1 after a similar pact, which was introduced at the start of last year, expires at the end of March.

"We already sent the proposal of a new agreement to the Office for Protection of Competition, and we expect the office will approve it by the end of March," Srecko Korber, head of the association, told Reuters.
He said lending rates were expected to follow the suggested decrease in deposit interest rates.
"Last year, lending rates dropped accordingly, and we expect the same to happen this year," Korber said. "We believe the level of interest rates in Slovenia is still too high."
Average interest rates for tolar deposits of between 31 and 90 days were at 4.8 percent in October, the last month for which figures were available, down from 6.3 percent a year earlier.
Interest rates on short-term capital loans decreased to 11.7 percent from 12.7 percent in the same month of 1995. -- Marja Novak, Ljubljana newsroom, 386-61-125-8439
